correctness.rationale: For the harvested Hutchinson DDE dx/dt=(r/K)x(t)[Kδ−x(t−τ)] on continuous strictly positive histories, compact support of a stationary invariant measure gives uniform upper/lower bounds on X0; every continuous φ on its range has a C¹ primitive H with H'(u)=Kφ(u)/(ru). Along any trajectory dH(x(t))/dt=φ(X0)[Kδ−X_{−τ}]. Invariance and bounded dominated time-difference quotient give E[φ(X0)(Kδ−X_{−τ})]=0; by density of continuous functions this is E[X_{−τ}|X0]=Kδ. Strictly positive delayed coordinate forces Kδ>0, hence δ<r. Invariance at time τ identifies X_{−τ} and X0 marginals, so E[X0]=Kδ, E[X0X_{−τ}]=Kδ², Cov(X0,X_{−τ})=0. Identity (xdot/x)=(r/K)(Kδ−X_{−τ}) implies Var(X0)=(K/r)² E[(xdot/x)²]. If variance zero, forward invariance and continuity make the entire future path constant; DDE on [0,τ] then makes its entire history constant, so only equilibrium atom. For every other compact stationary law positive variance and exact mean force mass strictly on either side of Kδ; a continuous nonconstant periodic orbit must cross it at least twice. Exact rational rederivation r=2,K=3,δ=1/2 yielded Kδ=9/4 and checked pointwise rewrite for four delayed states. Existence of nontrivial stationary measures is not asserted.
